title: Algebraic spaces over S as algebraic spaces over a smaller base with a map to S
statement: Let $g:S\to S'$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]; the case used most is $S'=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. For an algebraic space $X$ over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] define the sheaf $j_!X$ on the big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/S')_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site] by $j_!X(T)=\coprod_{\varphi:T\to S}X(T\xrightarrow{\varphi}S)$ for $S'$-schemes $T$, with its evident map $j_!X\to h_S$. Then the following hold. (1) $j_!X$ is an algebraic space over $S'$; if $U$ is a scheme over $S$ with a surjective etale map $h_U\to X$, then $U$, viewed as a scheme over $S'$, has a surjective etale map to $j_!X$; and for every diagram $X\to Z\leftarrow Y$ of algebraic spaces over $S$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] the canonical map $j_!(X\times_ZY)\to j_!X\times_{j_!Z}j_!Y$ is an isomorphism. (2) The functor $X\mapsto(j_!X,\,j_!X\to S)$ is an equivalence from the category of algebraic spaces over $S$ to the category of pairs $(F,F\to S)$ consisting of an algebraic space $F$ over $S'$ and a morphism $F\to S$ of algebraic spaces over $S'$; morphisms of pairs are morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S'$ commuting with the maps to $S$. (3) Viewing schemes over $S$ as schemes over $S'$ identifies the small etale site of $X$ with that of $j_!X$ (objects, morphisms and coverings) and identifies their structure sheaves. For a morphism $h:X\to Y$ of algebraic spaces over $S$, these identifications carry the functor $V\mapsto V\times_YX$ on etale scheme objects over $Y$ to the same functor for $j_!h$. No finiteness or separation hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Work in one common big fppf site containing both bases, with its small skeleton in the larger universe. The category of schemes over $S$ identifies with the slice of schemes over $S'$ at $S$: an object is a map $T\to S$, and morphisms and coverings are unchanged. The localized-sheaf equivalence therefore applies. Here $h_S$ is already a sheaf, by the scheme-as-algebraic-space node. Moreover its extension presheaf is already a sheaf: on a covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ a matching family $(\varphi_i,x_i)$ first glues uniquely to $\varphi:T\to S$ because $h_S$ is a sheaf, and then the $x_i$ glue uniquely by the sheaf condition for $X$ on the covering of $(T,\varphi)$. Thus the displayed formula in the statement is the extension sheaf itself. The cited equivalence identifies all sheaves over $S$ with pairs $(F,p:F\to h_S)$; its inverse is $G(T,\varphi)=\{x\in F(T):p(x)=\varphi\}$.

proof.text: For a scheme $U/S$, the map $(\varphi,a)\mapsto a$ identifies $j_!h_U(T)$ with $\operatorname{Mor}_{S'}(T,U)$: the inverse equips $a:T\to U$ with the forced structure map $\varphi=(U\to S)\circ a$. For a diagram of sheaves $A\to C\leftarrow B$ on $S$, an element of $j_!A(T)\times_{j_!C(T)}j_!B(T)$ is exactly a pair $((\varphi,a),(\varphi,b))$ with equal images in $C(T,\varphi)$. It corresponds to $(\varphi,(a,b))$ in $j_!(A\times_CB)(T)$. These inverse formulas commute with restrictions and projections. Sectionwise computation of sheaf limits makes this the asserted canonical fibre-product isomorphism. In particular it preserves the given diagram, not products over an unrelated terminal base.

source.place: Tag 03HU (lemma-describe-j-shriek-representable); Tag 04BB (lemma-j-shriek-commutes-equalizers-fibre-products), via the explicit formula; spaces.tex Tag 03I4

proof.text: We verify algebraicity directly from its definition. For two schemes $A,B$ with maps to $j_!X$, their composites with $j_!X\to h_S$ equip them with $S$-structures and maps to $X$. Their fibre sheaf over $j_!X$ is represented by the same scheme $P=A\times_X B$ as over $S$: on any $S'$-test scheme equality of the two images forces the induced maps to $S$ to agree, and the remaining equality is exactly equality in $X$. The scheme $P$ exists since it is the pullback of the representable diagonal of $X$ along $A\times_S B\to X\times X$. To test the diagonal of $j_!X$ on an arbitrary $T\to j_!X\times j_!X$, use two copies $A,B$ of $T$ with their possibly different induced $S$-structures. Its pullback is $T\times_{T\times_{S'}T}P$, where $T$ maps diagonally to $T\times_{S'}T$. Scheme fibre products show this is representable; no closedness of a diagonal is needed. Finally let $U\to X$ be the given etale surjective scheme atlas. A map $T\to j_!X$ determines a single $S$-structure on $T$, and $T\times_{j_!X}U=T\times_XU$ with the same projection to $T$. This is a scheme and its projection is etale and surjective by the atlas hypothesis. Thus $j_!X$ is algebraic and this particular $U$ remains an atlas. Together with step 2 this proves (1).

source.place: Tag 025Y (definition-algebraic-space); Tag 03I4 (lemma-change-base-scheme), part (3), with the representability tests written out

proof.text: Conversely let $F$ be an algebraic space over $S'$ with a map $p:F\to h_S$, and take its inverse sheaf $G$ from step 1. For a scheme $T/S$ and two sections of $G(T)$, equality is exactly equality of their images in $F(T)$; consequently the scheme representing their equality subfunctor (the pullback of the diagonal of $F$) also represents the pullback of the diagonal of $G$. It inherits its map to $S$ from $T$. Hence the diagonal of $G$ is representable. Choose an etale surjective atlas $U\to F$. The composite $h_U\to F\to h_S$ gives $U$ an $S$-structure and a map $h_{U/S}\to G$ (evaluate the composite on the identity of $U$; naturality forces every other component). For each $T/S\to G$, the sheaf $T\times_GU$ is exactly the fibre product $T\times_FU$ over $S'$: equality of the two sections in $F$ already forces equality of their maps to $S$. The latter is a scheme etale and surjective over $T$. Thus $G$ is algebraic. Steps 3 and 4 show that the equivalence of step 1 restricts to precisely the two full subcategories in (2); its inverse maps, unit and counit restrict as well. This proves all of (2).

source.place: Tag 04SG (lemma-category-of-spaces-over-smaller-base-scheme), restriction of the sheaf equivalence; explicit diagonal and atlas verification

proof.text: If $V/S\to X$ is a scheme object, its image $V/S'\to j_!X$ is etale exactly when the original map is: for every scheme test $T\to j_!X$, step 3 identifies its pullback projection with the original test on the uniquely induced $S$-scheme $T$. Conversely every $S$-test occurs this way. An arbitrary scheme object $V/S'\to j_!X$ acquires its unique $S$-structure by composition with $h_S$ and hence comes from an object over $X$; the etale test just given works in both directions. Maps between these objects over $j_!X$ automatically commute with their maps to $S$, so they are precisely the maps over $X$. Both constructions act as the identity on the underlying scheme maps. Coverings in these small sites are jointly surjective etale families of those same scheme maps, so coverings agree. The formula $\mathcal O(V)=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ is identical, and on a scheme arrow its restriction is the very same pullback on regular functions. This identifies the sites with their structure sheaves, as asserted in (3).

source.place: Tag 04KK (lemma-2-morphism), first paragraph of proof; spaces.tex Tag 03I5 (definition-base-change) and the test calculation of Tag 03I6 (lemma-viewed-as-properties)

proof.text: For $h:X\to Y$ over $S$ and an etale scheme $V\to Y$, the object $V\times_YX$ is the sheaf fibre product over $S$; it need not be a scheme (for $V=Y=S$ it is $X$ itself), so the comparison is made through its projection to $X$. This projection is representable and etale: for a scheme $T\to X$ the fibre $T\times_X(V\times_YX)=T\times_YV$ is a scheme etale over $T$, because $V\to Y$ is representable etale [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Step 2 gives $j_!(V\times_YX)\simeq V\times_{j_!Y}j_!X$, compatibly with both projections and natural in arrows of $V$, since the pair formulas commute with restriction. For a scheme test $T\to j_!X$, with its uniquely induced $S$-structure, the fibre of $V\times_{j_!Y}j_!X\to j_!X$ is $T\times_{j_!Y}V=T\times_YV$: test sections are pairs with equal images in $j_!Y$, and that equality already includes equality of the maps to $S$. So both projections have the same scheme tests with the same projections to $T$. When $V\times_YX$ is a scheme (an object of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$), its image under step 5 is $V\times_{j_!Y}j_!X$, by the representable formula of step 2. Thus the base-change functors agree on objects and on morphisms, and their maps on regular functions are the same scheme pullbacks. No assertion above used finiteness or separation, which proves the final clause.

lean.note: The extension functor is specified by the exact sigma formula, the projection, restrictions and action on morphisms. The theorem also gives its equivalence with spaces mapping to S, retention of each given atlas, preservation of sheaf pullback squares, and a scheme-chart-normalized equivalence of small etale ringed sites. Preservation of all pullback squares, together with that chart normalization, expresses the canonical fibre-product comparison naturally in the etale scheme object, including when the fibre product is not itself a scheme.
